result: Of 445 tertiary referral patients surveyed about 1.5 years after evaluation, 64% reported improvement but only 2% complete resolution; CDC-defined CFS had worse severity and function at follow-up than chronic fatigue, and dysthymia predicted less improvement.
reason: Independent cohort measuring full recovery and improvement rates; low recovery matches the finding.

result: Baseline circulating cortisol was lowest in CFS (n=10), intermediate in 25 matched controls and highest in major depression (n=15) (P=0.01); prolactin response to d-fenfluramine was higher in CFS than controls (P=0.05).
reason: Measures baseline cortisol, lower in CFS than controls; very small sample and blood rather than free cortisol, so weak support.

result: At a mean 3.2 years after trial entry, 63% of 103 CFS patients had improved but only 6% were symptom-free; 30% could not work and 25% were on disability benefit; cell-mediated immunity did not predict outcome.
reason: Independent follow-up cohort; 6% full recovery and 63% improvement fit the low-recovery claim.

result: Blinded, quantified electron microscopy of needle muscle biopsies from 15 CFS patients and 15 matched controls found no difference in subsarcolemmal or intermyofibrillar mitochondrial aggregates, mitochondrial size, pleomorphism or inner-membrane compartmentalisation.
reason: Independent blinded biopsy study with normal mitochondrial ultrastructure, as in Lane 1998 EM; argues against Behan 1991.

result: In 76 patients with disabling unexplained fatigue and 76 matched controls, enterovirus serology and VP1 antigen testing did not differ, no enterovirus grew from stool culture, and stool PCR was positive in one patient only, and not on a repeat sample 3 months later.
reason: Tests serology and stool, not stomach biopsy VP1/RNA, so it does not test the finding's measure; no atlas finding covers blood or stool enterovirus.

result: In a placebo-controlled poly(I)-poly(C12U) trial, PBMC bioactive 2-5A (p<0.0001) and RNase L activity (p=0.001) were raised at baseline vs controls; in those with high baseline RNase L, treatment lowered RNase L (p=0.005) and 2-5A (p=0.09), and the RNase L fall correlated with cognitive improvement (p=0.007).
reason: Same measure and direction but from the same lab and likely overlapping trial patients, so not independent; adds treatment-response data. Appears to be the In Vivo 1994 paper rather than the cited Clin Infect Dis 1994 paper.

result: In an earlier randomised placebo-controlled rintatolimod trial, treatment lowered PBMC RNase L activity (p=0.005) in patients with high baseline levels, and the fall correlated with cognitive improvement (p=0.007).
reason: Earlier trial of the same drug; gives mechanistic biomarker data, not replication of the phase III treadmill result, and no efficacy numbers in the abstract.

result: 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT showed 6.53 regional perfusion defects per patient in 45 CFS patients vs 1.66 in 38 healthy controls (similar to 6.43 in unipolar depression), mainly frontal and temporal, with a lower midcerebral uptake index in CFS.
reason: Resting SPECT perfusion lower in CFS; not specific vs depression, which fits the contested framing; orthostatic status not recorded.

result: Resting serum TGF-beta was higher in 10 CFS patients than 10 controls (287 vs 115 pg/ml, P<0.01); IL-1 beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were undetectable before and after 30 min of walking at 1 mph, and the post-exercise rise in TGF-beta was not significant vs controls.
reason: Reports a TGF-beta elevation (one of the tallied positives) but does not test blood handling; fits the meta-analysis TGF-beta elevation, and is an example of what the artefact finding undercuts (serum, handling not stated).

result: After 30 min of walking at 1 mph, SPECT cerebral blood flow abnormalities seemed larger in 10 CFS patients, but they did not differ significantly from 10 controls.
reason: Too thin: the abstract gives no resting CBF comparison and the post-exercise change was not significant; no atlas finding covers exertion-induced CBF.
